article.dek: Jacksonville covered and the total went over on Thursday night, the board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, and Friday's final injury designations are the next thing that can move a Sunday price.

items.headline: Lead: Jaguars 33, Ravens 10 — Jacksonville covered, the total went over
paragraphs: Thursday night went the way the market expected it to, only louder. Jacksonville beat Baltimore 33-10 at M&T Bank Stadium, covering the closing line of 10 and pushing the total over 39.5 with 43 points scored.

Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown, and Bhayshul Tuten scored on the opening drive after being a game-time call with ankle and foot injuries. The Jaguars held Derrick Henry to 57 yards on 17 carries and forced three Baltimore turnovers.

For Baltimore, rookie Joe Fagnano went 10 of 18 with two second-half interceptions in his first career start. The Ravens fall to 4-5 with their fourth straight loss. Jacksonville improves to 6-2 and now gets ten days off before its next game at Tennessee.
The rain showed up as forecast. It was a wet night in Baltimore, and the weather did not slow Jacksonville down.
items.takeaway: Jacksonville won 33-10 on Thursday night, covering the 10-point line and sending the total over 39.5.

items.headline: Sunday quarterback picture: Darnold out, Lock starts; Milton starts for Philadelphia
paragraphs: Nothing changed overnight on the two Sunday quarterback calls that matter. Seattle is still without Sam Darnold against Arizona — he is out with a quad injury, week-to-week, and will not go on injured reserve. Drew Lock starts in his place. Lock has been limited in practice for two weeks with an elbow injury of his own, so Seattle plans to manage his throwing workload.

In Philadelphia, Joe Milton still starts at quarterback Sunday against the Giants. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots. Tanner McKee, who has a chest injury but was a full participant, is the backup.

Friday's final injury designations land later today. That is the next real information event for Sunday. Inactives come about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday, so the morning brief cannot have them — watch for the designations this afternoon and the inactive lists Sunday.
items.takeaway: Darnold is out and Lock starts for Seattle; Milton starts for Philadelphia — and Friday's final designations are the next update to watch.

items.headline: Weather: no real weather problem anywhere on Sunday
paragraphs: Sunday looks calm almost everywhere. No outdoor game carries a real weather downgrade. The windiest spots are Seattle and New England, and even those are mild.

Arizona at Seattle, 4:25 p.m. ET at Lumen Field, has the week's strongest wind: about 10 to 14 miles per hour out of the south-southwest, gusting to 25, around 56 degrees, with a slight chance of light rain. Green Bay at New England, also 4:25 p.m. ET, is similar — wind near 12 miles per hour gusting to 25, around 51 degrees, mostly clear.

Everywhere else is quiet. The Jets at Kansas City is near 60 degrees and clear with a light wind. Detroit at Miami is the warmest game of the week, in the low 80s. The Bengals and Falcons play in Madrid at 9:30 a.m. ET under a retractable roof, around 60 degrees and cloudy. Dallas at Indianapolis is under a retractable roof too, and Cleveland at New Orleans and Houston at the Chargers are indoors.
That is a factual weather read, not a totals edge. Wind is the weather that matters most for football, and nothing on this slate is strong enough to build a bet around on its own.
items.takeaway: Sunday is calm: the windiest games are Seattle and New England with gusts to 25, and nothing else is close to a weather problem.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: Read Friday morning, the app board still shows Week 8, generated November 2. There are no Week 9 cards at all. Its Baltimore game is still the Week 8 trip to Buffalo, and its quarterback field is blank — it has not picked up Fagnano as Thursday's starter, let alone the Sunday quarterbacks.

So there is still no Sunday card to read, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. If your book has a Sunday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

The only cards on the board are Monday's Chicago at Seattle game, which has already been played. They are worth one look because they show how the three cards differ. The Value card and the Balanced card were the same play: Chicago +3 at -102, with the model giving Chicago a 50.6% chance against a market price implying 46.5% — a +3.6% edge. The Hit Rate card was Seattle on the moneyline at -175, with the model at 56.1% against a market price implying 60.4%. Hit Rate is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It is not the best value. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Sunday's prices go through Check until the board flips.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers — why 3 and 7 matter more than other numbers
paragraphs: A key number is a final margin that games land on more often than other margins. In the NFL, 3 and 7 are the big ones, because a field goal is worth 3 and a touchdown with the extra point is worth 7. Games end by exactly 3 or exactly 7 far more often than they end by 4, 5, or 6.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say a favorite is -3.5. If the favorite wins by exactly 3, a bet on the favorite loses, but a bet on the favorite at -2.5 would have won. That half-point, from -3.5 to -2.5, crosses the key number 3. It is worth more than a half-point anywhere else.

Why it matters: when you shop lines, the price around a key number matters. Getting -2.5 instead of -3.5 on a favorite, or +3.5 instead of +2.5 on an underdog, is a real improvement — not just a slightly better price. That is also why books charge more juice to move across 3 or 7.
items.takeaway: Games land on 3 and 7 more than any other margin, so a half-point across a key number is worth more than a half-point anywhere else.

items.headline: Thursday closed at Jacksonville -10 and the favorite covered; Houston ticked up overnight
paragraphs: Thursday's line settled where the evening brief left it: Jacksonville -10 at DraftKings with the total at 39.5. The final was 33-10, so the favorite covered by 13 and the total went over by three and a half points. A week ago the lookahead had Baltimore as a 3-point favorite with a total of 48.5 — the quarterback injuries flipped the favorite and pulled the total down about nine points.

The Sunday board moved a little overnight. Houston went from -4.5 to -5.5 at the Chargers. The 49ers-Raiders total ticked down a point to 51.5, and the Packers-Patriots total ticked down to 44.5. Dallas ticked to -5 at Indianapolis. The rest of the board held: Cincinnati -3 at Atlanta in Madrid with the week's highest total at 52.5, Detroit -7 at Miami, Kansas City -9.5 against the Jets, and Seattle still -8.5 against Arizona after the three-point Darnold move earlier in the week.

The app has not caught any of it yet. The board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, so none of these prices are on a card. If your book has a line you like, run it through Check: type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Jacksonville covered -10 and the total went over Thursday; overnight, Houston moved to -5.5 and two totals ticked down a point.

items.headline: Wait for Friday's designations — then bet the good number now
paragraphs: Friday's final injury designations are the one real information event left before Sunday. That is the thing worth waiting for on a Sunday price. Once they land this afternoon, there is nothing else to wait on — inactives do not come until about 90 minutes before kickoff.

And once the designations are in, do not keep waiting. If your book has a Sunday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number Sunday, because the Sunday late rush on big-name teams can push the line the wrong way. A quick price reminder: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be.
One honesty note while we are here: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Wait for Friday's final designations this afternoon, then run your book's Sunday price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now.
